q: Quantum simulation of chemistry (the electronic structure problem): the N-electron molecule problem is QMA-complete in general, but variational methods (VQE) approximate ground states. The main challenge is that the Hilbert space dimension grows as:
opts: Exponentially: O(2^N) (the full Hilbert space of N two-level systems)
exp: The N-electron Hilbert space (with M spin-orbitals) has dimension C(M,N) ≈ 2^{M} — exponentially large. Classical methods (FCI = full configuration interaction) are exact but exponentially expensive. Quantum computers can represent the N-electron state in O(M) qubits, potentially giving exponential speedup.
